title: Stochastic Primal-Dual Decoding for Multiobjective Generative Recommender Systems

problem.claim: Generative recommender systems must construct ordered item slates that satisfy multiple objectives beyond relevance, including item-attribute and fairness constraints.

gap.claim: Existing approaches either use post-processing that does not explicitly account for the sequential nature of generative recommendation or add auxiliary objectives during training, which is often impractical at large scale.

narrative_sequence.summary: Generative modelling has produced substantial performance gains in recommender systems.
Recommendation requires constructing ordered slates that meet multiple objectives, including attribute-based and fairness constraints.
Current multiobjective methods use either post-processing for non-generative settings or auxiliary objectives incorporated into model training.
Post-processing does not explicitly model sequential generation, while training with auxiliary objectives is often impractical for large-scale systems.

source_observation.claim: Multiobjective recommendation methods should account for the sequential nature of generative slate construction.

interpretation.claim: Methods designed for non-generative post-processing may miss constraints arising during sequential generation.

application.claim: When designing multiobjective generative recommenders, integrate objective handling with sequential decoding rather than relying only on post-processing.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this design is effective across particular constraints, datasets, or system scales.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the proposed method's algorithmic details.
The abstract does not report datasets, baselines, quantitative results, or computational costs.
